title: Do not add an Accept-Language auto-redirect between / and /en/; the language switch stays a plain link
body: Spanish lives at / and English at /en/, chosen by the reader through LocaleSwitch.astro, which is a plain <a> to the other locale's home (works without JS; /cv and /en/cv ship zero JS). Automatic redirection by Accept-Language was rejected in the 2026-09-02 en-site spec: it breaks the back button, it hides Spanish from a reader whose browser says English but who wants Spanish (the market is LatAm and Spanish is canonical), and on a static host it costs a redirect rule (a Function or _redirects) in front of every request. x-default in hreflang points at Spanish for the same reason. Do not add a redirect in functions/, public/_headers, a new public/_redirects, or a client script.
not_derivable: Nothing in code or remaining docs records that auto-redirect was considered and rejected, or why; an agent 'improving' i18n would plausibly add it.

evidence.summary: The ES/EN switch: a link, not a script, pointing at the other locale's home.
Rejection and reasons from the deleted docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-02-en-site-design.md §2.4-2.5.
